$comment: The fleet manifest (docs/MECHANIZATION_PLAYBOOK.md, Conversion 3) — the single source of the metro fleet, served at https://chidistricts.com/metros.json by the Pages deploy. Runtime behavior is deliberately unchanged: the app never fetches this file. It is consumed at GENERATION time — `generate_metro_files.py --sync-fleet` projects these entries (minus `repo`) into each fork's worksheet metro_explorers, and the weekly fleet-status workflow reads `repo` to aggregate across forks. Launching metro N+1 means: add its entry here, then run --sync-fleet + regenerate in each fork (a regeneration PR, never a hand edit). The `tag`, `landing_name` and `blurb` fields drive the ROOT LANDING PAGE (scripts/build_landing_page.py) and are deliberately fleet-level: sync_fleet projects a whitelist into each worksheet's metro_explorers, so these three never reach an app. `tag` is the instance tag the brand spec sets in the wordmark (districtry / il); `landing_name` is the AREA a reader picks, which is not always the metro label — the Illinois instance is listed as Illinois because it serves 89 counties, while its metro label stays Chicago for the app's own sibling-metro portal. `url` is what the landing page links: at R5 these become districtry.com paths, and the page follows automatically.

metros.label: Chicago
metros.blurb: 89 counties. Wards, county boards, police districts and beats, school zones, judicial subcircuits, and the people who hold those seats.

metros.label: New York City
metros.blurb: Boroughs, City Council and community districts, NYPD precincts and sectors, school zones, and the state and federal seats above them.

metros.label: San Francisco
metros.blurb: Supervisor districts, neighborhoods, police districts, school attendance areas, and the state and federal seats above them.
